_doc: Investment-cost model for datacenter_v1, grounded in the real playbook config (config/playbooks/datacenter_v1.json, 4 of 4 covered) and the real pillar catalog (config/datacenter_v1_kpi_catalog.json). Companion to config/economics/datacenter_v1.json: economics answers 'what is a point worth', this answers 'what does it cost to move one'. Same discipline as config/investment/saas_premium.json: every figure carries {value, basis}, and a figure computed from two assumed inputs is itself 'assumed' (roi.basis.money()'s weakest-link rule), never 'derived' just because arithmetic was involved.

csm_hourly_cost.basis: assumed: blended fully-loaded CSM/CS-ops hourly cost (salary + overhead / annual working hours), same figure as every other vertical's file — CSM cost doesn't vary by vertical the way retention sensitivity does (config/investment/saas_premium.json's own basis sentence).

_playbooks_doc: Grounded in config/playbooks/datacenter_v1.json's 4 real playbooks and their real action_class/trigger roles. targets_pillars is resolved mechanically where possible (power_of_1.json's attribution.signal_role_to_pillar_role crossed with this catalog's pillar_roles) and cross-checked by hand; where a role names a KPI unambiguously (e.g. an infra incident threatening SLA attainment) a specific targets_kpis entry is claimed, same discipline as saas_premium. estimated_health_point_lift_per_execution is a placeholder ONLY until roi.measured's per-playbook sensitivity (>=5 closed interventions with both a health lift and a revenue outcome) exists for that playbook.

estimated_csm_hours.basis: assumed: incident triage with the infra/NOC team + a customer exec update call + resolution follow-through + a wrap-up report, for an 'escalate' action_class playbook on a live infrastructure incident

estimated_cost_per_execution.basis: assumed: estimated_csm_hours (assumed) x csm_hourly_cost (assumed) — both links assumed, so the product is assumed, not derived

estimated_health_point_lift_per_executio.basis: assumed: informal CS-leadership estimate for a resolved infrastructure incident's effect on P3 (Reliability & SLA Delivery); no datacenter_v1 tenant yet has >=5 closed instances of this playbook with both a measured lift and a revenue outcome — replace with roi.measured's sensitivity figure once one does

estimated_csm_hours.basis: assumed: capacity/utilization analysis + a pricing proposal for additional reserved capacity + a presentation call + a follow-up, 'offer' action_class

estimated_health_point_lift_per_executio.note: this playbook's expected_outcome is entirely expansion/commercial (expansion_closed, expansion_opportunity, repeat_order) — no health-score outcome type. The $ value belongs in expansion revenue, not a point-lift figure, even though the playbook also touches the capacity pillar (P2) conceptually via its capacity_pressure trigger role. Left null rather than forced into a shape that doesn't fit, mirroring saas_premium's expansion_intent_handoff.

estimated_csm_hours.basis: assumed: a unit-economics/usage review + a pricing or terms conversation under budget pressure + a follow-up, 'schedule' action_class

estimated_health_point_lift_per_executio.basis: assumed: informal CS-leadership estimate — this playbook protects revenue/unit-economics under commercial pressure more than it lifts a health score; treat this figure as low-confidence pending real closed-instance data, same caveat as saas_premium's seat_truedown_save

estimated_csm_hours.basis: assumed: qualify the signal + warm handoff to sales, 'notify' action_class — the lightest-touch playbook in this catalog

estimated_health_point_lift_per_executio.note: this playbook's expected_outcome is expansion revenue, not a health-score lift — same shape as saas_premium's expansion_intent_handoff. Left null rather than forced.

_pillars_doc: Pillar-level cost rolls up from the playbooks that target it — no separate flat number. A pillar with no targeting playbook is shown as not_covered, not guessed.

P1.name: Revenue & Unit Economics
P1.note: one playbook covers this pillar; cost-per-point should be computed at query time as estimated_cost_per_execution / (measured lift if roi.measured has >=5 qualifying closed instances, else estimated_health_point_lift_per_execution) — not pre-computed and stored here

P2.name: Fleet Utilization & Goodput
P2.note: one playbook touches this pillar conceptually (capacity_pressure is one of its two trigger roles) but its tracked outcome is expansion revenue, not a health-point lift — see the playbook's own null lift note

P3.name: Reliability & SLA Delivery
P3.note: one playbook covers this pillar, targeting SLA attainment (P3-KPI6) specifically — an infrastructure incident is escalated precisely because it threatens SLA attainment

P4.name: Power & Facility
P4.note: no playbook in config/playbooks/datacenter_v1.json targets a P4 signal role (power/facility/thermal issues are folded into the generic infra_incident role that incident_escalation already covers under P3, not tracked as a separate P4 trigger). This catalog's own pillar_roles_notes confirms P4 is deliberately unmapped from the shared role vocabulary. Absent, not guessed, until a playbook exists or someone authors a standalone assumption for it.

P5.name: Commercial & Expansion
P5.note: two playbooks target this pillar; both are grow-lens plays with expansion-revenue outcomes, not health-point lifts — their costs are not summed into one 'P5 cost' figure, report them side by side, same as saas_premium's P5 rule

P6.name: Provisioning Velocity
P6.note: no playbook in config/playbooks/datacenter_v1.json targets the 'adoption' role this pillar plays (config/datacenter_v1_kpi_catalog.json's own pillar_roles_notes already flags P6's adoption mapping as a moderate-confidence analogy, not a firm one) — absent, not guessed.

_kpis_doc: KPI-level entries exist only for KPIs a playbook actually names in targets_kpis — same non-guessing rule as pillars.

P3-KPI6.name: SLA attainment
P3-KPI6.note: inherits its one playbook's cost/lift figures directly; no KPI-specific override authored yet

P5-KPI4.name: Expansion probability (90d)
P5-KPI4.note: inherits its one playbook's cost figures; no health-point lift (this KPI moves on the expansion-revenue side, not a health score)
